strategies.summary: After price trades into a higher-timeframe PD array, wait for a liquidity sweep that breaks the opposing swing with a wick and leaves a fair value gap. Enter on the retracement that respects that confirming gap and target the opposing higher-timeframe objective.

timeframes.notes: Fractal higher-timeframe array plus execution-chart model. The examples show 1d->15m and 1h/15m->5m, but the presenter teaches the pattern as transferable across timeframe ladders.

glossary.EXTERNAL_MOVE: The liquidity-taking sweep into the higher-timeframe array; machine proxy = structural_event.kind liquidity_sweep_low/high on the setup chart.
glossary.INTERNAL_MOVE: The rebalancing leg that breaks the opposing swing with a wick, leaves a fair value gap, and then respects that gap on the retrace.
glossary.LINE_OF_DEFENSE: The higher-timeframe PD array expected to hold the reversal; the machine proxy is custom_signals.htf_pd_array_tap on bias_tf.

custom_signals.name: htf_pd_array_tap
custom_signals.plain_definition: Price trades into a higher-timeframe discount array (bullish) or premium array (bearish), such as a fair value gap or order block.
custom_signals.numeric_definition: (low <= bullish_fvg[0].gap_high@bias_tf AND high >= bullish_fvg[0].gap_low@bias_tf AND NOT bullish_fvg[0].filled@bias_tf) OR (low <= bullish_ob[0].zone_high@bias_tf AND high >= bullish_ob[0].zone_low@bias_tf AND NOT bullish_ob[0].invalidated@bias_tf)

custom_signals.name: fvg_touched
custom_signals.plain_definition: Price trades into the fair value gap (a touch or sting), without requiring the consequent encroachment.

custom_signals.name: htf_opposing_pd_array
custom_signals.plain_definition: The opposing higher-timeframe premium array (for longs) that acts as the draw on liquidity.

custom_signals.name: short_term_high
custom_signals.plain_definition: A standard swing high (three-candle rule) that is not an intermediate term high.

sequence: Mark the higher-timeframe PD array that should defend the reversal.
Wait for price to sweep liquidity into that array on the execution chart.
Require the next leg to wick through the opposing swing and leave a bullish fair value gap.
Buy the retracement that respects that fair value gap.
Target the opposing higher-timeframe premium array or swing objective.

invalidation.text: If the impulsive leg fails to create a fair value gap, the swing extreme is likely to be swept again, invalidating the shift.
If price trades completely through the HTF line of defense or closes through the opposing edge of the internal order block/breaker.

filters.text: Do not enter if there is no fair value gap in the shift leg, because price is taking liquidity rather than rebalancing.
If an initial external move fails or occurs outside prime kill zones (e.g., early London), wait for a secondary external sweep followed by a clean internal move before entering.

entry_rule.text: Enter on the retracement into the confirming bullish fair value gap; if a breaker or order block overlaps it, use that overlap only as a refinement of the same gap-based entry.
entry_rule.quote: then we have a new internal and right there could be your entry right there

target_rule.text: Target the opposing higher-timeframe premium array first, then any remaining swing-high draw on liquidity beyond it.
target_rule.quote: this is actually your first premium array so this would be your first Target

stop_rule.text: Place the stop beyond the sweep candle low that made the external move.

management.partials: Take partial profits at the first premium array, letting remaining position run to secondary HTF target.
management.notes: Presenter notes that in high momentum, the first target is the immediate premium array, and the second target is the next draw on liquidity.

presenter_claims.claim: When we have fair value gaps up in the leg, they are more likely to hold and more likely to have an internal move than an external move.
When we break that swing high with that little wick right there, we don't have to close above it necessarily, that is your market structure shift.
Price is either rebalancing or taking liquidity; if it is not rebalancing something, then it is taking liquidity.

strategies.notes: The presenter's market structure shift is modeled as a wick break of the most recent confirmed swing rather than the engine's body-close CHoCH/BOS event. The higher-timeframe line of defense is proxied by custom_signals.htf_pd_array_tap, and the machine entry uses the confirming FVG's near edge even when the narration also mentions breaker or order-block overlap.

signals_observed.bias_source: Daily timeframe in high momentum returning to a FVG

setup_walkthrough.what_happens: Price trades into a Daily fair value gap acting as the first line of defense.
Price sweeps an intermediate swing low, executing an external move (turtle soup).
Price breaks above the previous swing high with a wick, creating a market structure shift.
A fair value gap is left behind in the upward leg, confirming an internal move.
Price retraces into the internal breaker and FVG, respecting it to continue higher.

examples.presenter_commentary: He emphasizes that an external move is a sweep of liquidity (turtle soup), while an internal move is the respect of a fair value gap or order block. The presence of the FVG in the leg up confirms the shift from external to internal.

may_differ.reason: The presenter explicitly accepts a wick break as the structure shift here, whereas the engine's CHoCH still needs a body close through the protected high.

signals_observed.bias_source: Reaction to HTF OB and FVG after sweeping a high

setup_walkthrough.what_happens: Price sweeps a high (external move) and leaves an FVG and OB lower.
Price returns to the OB and executes a 'trick' external move that drops but lacks an internal FVG confirmation in the leg.
A real external move sweeps highs again, followed by a real internal move that leaves a clean FVG.
Price retraces into the newly confirmed internal FVG, offering a valid short entry.

examples.presenter_commentary: He uses this bearish example to illustrate a 'trick' external move that fails. He emphasizes waiting for the internal move (a verified FVG in the displacement leg) to form after the external sweep before taking the entry, avoiding being caught in a false shift.
